In And Circumcenter D

GeometryTrianglesCircles
Game: A triangle and a circle build a second triangle; watch whether the two triangles are the same shape, with nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Drag A, B or C, or focus a point and use the arrow keys. Tick the boxes to show names, equal sides, angle marks or helper lines.

Keyboard: Tab to a corner, then use the arrow keys (Shift makes a bigger step).

Look for the math

A problem from Kvant takes a triangle, lays its side AB along the two other sides, and draws a circle through one centre around the other. Two chords of that circle then draw a triangle at a completely different place. Why is it the same triangle?

Putting AB on the other sides

Write a = BC, b = AC and c = AB. Point D is placed on ray BC with BD = c, and E is on ray AC with AE = c. So CD = |a − c| and CE = |b − c|. The page writes these as a − c and b − c, which silently assumes AB is no longer than the other two sides; if AB is longer, D or E falls beyond C and the lengths must be read as positive. The original applet still draws those positions, and so does this port. Its incenter and circumcenter are marked I and O.

Two chords through O

Let I(O) be the circle centred at I that passes through O. The chord through O parallel to AC ends at N. The line from I perpendicular to AC meets that chord at L, and the perpendicular from the centre of a circle cuts a chord in half, so ON = 2·OL. Let I′ and O′ be the feet on AC. The incircle touches AC at I′, giving CI′ = (a + b − c)/2, while O′ is the midpoint of AC, giving CO′ = b/2. Hence O′I′ = |a − c|/2. Both OO′ and LI′ are perpendicular to AC while OL and O′I′ run along it, so O-L-I′-O′ is a rectangle and OL = O′I′. Therefore ON = |a − c| = CD. The same argument with BC gives OM = |b − c| = CE. The logic test checked both formulas on the start diagram and on thousands of triangles.

Why the two triangles match

The sides of angle DCE lie along BC and AC, while the sides of angle NOM are parallel to BC and AC, so the two angles agree. Together with the two equal side pairs above, that is the side-angle-side test for congruent triangles: CDE = ONM, just as the page claims. The test found no exception in 4,000 random configurations once a chord is long enough for the applet's one-pixel choice of its far end; for a chord under a pixel, Other() can pick O itself, and the drawn lengths then differ from the formula.

What is different here

The sibling applets ask for DE to be both perpendicular and equal to IO, with equality only when angle C is 30°. This applet asks a different question: the circle through O builds a congruent triangle for any triangle. The live cut-the-knot page now shows a GeoGebra figure instead of the Java applet; the archived 2007 page at the Wayback Machine embeds InAndCircumcenterD with ShowNames=0, so this port follows that Java program and the same written claim.

Try a triangle with AB almost as long as AC: the chord OM gets very short, and you can see the applet's one-pixel choice fail.
